**Group:** Zooplankton  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A siphonophore: a colonial cnidarian built from many specialised zooids (swimming bells, feeding and reproductive units) arranged along a common stem, giving an elongate chain-, ribbon-, or string-like appearance, often transparent and gelatinous. Key features: repeated modular zooids along a stem, elongate colonial form, gelatinous transparent tissue.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **ctenophora** | Ctenophores are single ovoid comb jellies; siphonophores are elongate colonies of repeated zooids along a stem. |
| **guinardia_dactyliosolen_cerataulina** | A diatom chain is a row of similar rigid silica cells; a siphonophore is a soft gelatinous colony of differentiated zooids. |
